newsitem.title: USA: US late spot heat slips, gasoline jumps after data.
newsitem.headline: US late spot heat slips, gasoline jumps after data.

text.p: U.S. spot distillate prices fell sharply but gasoline enjoyed moderate gains by late Wednesday amid new inventory data and keen buying interest on Gulf Coast products, players said.

NYMEX April gasoline futures settled 0.44 cent higher on the heels of API data released Tuesday showing an unexpected 1.3 million-barrel drop in stocks for the week ending February 28. New EIA data released Wednesday showed a somewhat larger draw of 2.3 million barrels.
Gulf Coast back-eighth-cycle "M2"-grade conventional unleaded gasoline was offered at 3.40 cents below the print, about 0.40 cent firmer than late Tuesday, players said.
"The API numbers played a big role and seasonal demand is starting to perk up," one Gulf gasoline trader said, adding daily demand had been hovering over 7.9 million barrels for the past few weeks.
New York Harbour gasoline diffs edged lower, traders said, with "M4" grade offered at 2.50 cents below the print.
Heating oil and diesel prices fell sharply as NYMEX heat settled 0.80 cent lower. Heat diffs were stable, but Gulf low sulphur diesel diffs firmed about 0.70 cent amid short covering, traders said.
((- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632))
